title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Sharia Islam Worship And Supplication

questions.question: What is the main claim made about the Law brought by the Prophet in this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as unmatched in excellence and lasting influence.

questions.question: How long does the passage say this Law has guided a large part of humanity?
questions.answer: For fourteen centuries.

questions.question: About how much of humanity does the passage say this Law governed?
questions.answer: One fifth of humanity.

questions.question: What two qualities are used to describe how this Law governed people?
questions.answer: It governed with justice and precision.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was the source of Islam that appeared through the Prophet?
questions.answer: It came through his actions, words, and inner state.

questions.question: Name two roles Islam played for people in each century according to the passage.
questions.answer: It served as a guide and a refuge.

questions.question: How did Islam affect people’s minds and hearts in the passage?
questions.answer: It taught their minds and gave light and purity to their hearts.

questions.question: How did Islam affect people’s souls and spirits according to the passage?
questions.answer: It trained and refined their souls and helped their spirits grow and advance.

questions.question: In worship, what made the Prophet stand out from everyone else?
questions.answer: He was the first and leading example in practicing every form of worship in his religion.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his piety and fear of Allah?
questions.answer: It says he was unmatched in them.

questions.question: How did he carry out worship while also facing constant struggle and busy activity?
questions.answer: He still fulfilled worship completely and with deep care.

questions.question: What is important about his worship not being based on imitation?
questions.answer: It shows his worship was original, complete, and directly sincere before Allah.

questions.question: What book of supplication is mentioned as showing his special rank in knowing Allah?
questions.answer: Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What does the passage say later saints and knowers of Allah could not reach, even together?
questions.answer: They could not reach his level in knowing and describing Allah.

questions.question: If later great spiritual people could not match him in prayer and knowledge of Allah, what does that help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove that he had no equal in supplication and spiritual knowledge.

questions.question: What is the central idea of this whole passage about the Prophet?
questions.answer: It argues that he had no equal in religion, worship, and prayer.

questions.question: Which six things does the passage say he brought that have no equal?
questions.answer: A sacred law, Islam, a way of worship, a cause, a call, and a faith.

questions.question: Why does the passage say no better form of these things could exist?
questions.answer: Because they are described as reaching the highest level of perfection.

questions.question: What fact from history is used to support the greatness of the Law he brought?
questions.answer: It ruled one fifth of humanity for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: How is Islam described as helping people intellectually?
questions.answer: It guided their minds and taught them.

questions.question: How is Islam described as helping people spiritually?
questions.answer: It purified hearts, trained souls, and raised spirits.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s place among worshippers?
questions.answer: He is shown as the top example and first practitioner of worship in his religion.

questions.question: What difficult condition did he face while still worshipping fully?
questions.answer: He was in ongoing struggle and constant activity.

questions.question: What does it mean that his worship joined the beginning and end of servitude beautifully?
questions.answer: It means his worship was complete, balanced, and excellent in every stage.

questions.question: What is Jawshan al-Kabir used to show in this passage?
questions.answer: It is used to show his unmatched depth in knowing and praising his Lord.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the Prophet and later saints and gnostics?
questions.answer: Even all of them together could not reach his level in this area.

questions.question: What part of the Treatise on Supplicatory Prayer is mentioned?
questions.answer: Its opening section that explains some meaning from one section of the Jawshan.

questions.question: What conclusion is a reader expected to reach after seeing that explanation?
questions.answer: That the Jawshan itself has no equal.

questions.question: According to the passage, what made the Prophet’s sacred law special among all laws?
questions.answer: No similar law exists, and none more perfect could exist.

questions.question: What detail shows that this law was not just theoretical?
questions.answer: It actually guided and governed a huge part of humanity over many centuries.

questions.question: Why is the phrase about one fifth of humanity important?
questions.answer: It shows the law had wide reach and real influence in human life.

questions.question: From what three things did the Islam mentioned in the passage come forth?
questions.answer: From his deeds, his speech, and his inward condition.

questions.question: Give two ways Islam served people besides giving rules.
questions.answer: It sheltered them and educated them.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam did for hearts?
questions.answer: It gave them light and cleansed them.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam did for souls?
questions.answer: It refined and trained them.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Prophet to worship practice?
questions.answer: It says he was ahead of everyone in carrying it out.

questions.question: Why is it meaningful that he worshipped perfectly without copying anyone?
questions.answer: It means his worship was original and came from his true mission and closeness to Allah.

questions.question: What is one reason Jawshan al-Kabir is important in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows how deeply he knew and described his Sustainer.

questions.question: How are later saints used as evidence here?
questions.answer: Their inability to match him makes his rank clearer.

questions.question: If a person studies the example from the Treatise on Supplicatory Prayer, what judgment does the passage expect?
questions.answer: That this supplication is also without equal.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the possibility of finding something equal to the religion-related things brought by the Prophet?
questions.answer: It says nothing equal to them exists or could exist.

questions.question: Which of these is included in that statement: worship, trade, medicine, or poetry?
questions.answer: Worship.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the long-term rule of the sacred law?
questions.answer: It describes it as fair, exact, and effective over many centuries.

questions.question: Who benefited from Islam in each century according to the passage?
questions.answer: Three hundred million people.

questions.question: What four areas of a person did Islam improve in the passage?
questions.answer: The mind, heart, soul, and spirit.

questions.question: What was the Prophet’s rank in carrying out the acts of worship in his religion?
questions.answer: He was the foremost and first in practicing them.

questions.question: Which two inner qualities especially marked his worship?
questions.answer: Strong piety and deep fear of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the completeness of his worship during difficult times?
questions.answer: He still performed it fully and carefully even while active and struggling.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that he did not imitate anyone in worship?
questions.answer: To show that his servitude to Allah was uniquely complete and genuine.

questions.question: What example from his prayers is given to show his unmatched spiritual rank?
questions.answer: The Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What does the passage claim about the combined efforts of later gnostics and saints?
questions.answer: Even together, they could not reach his level of knowing and describing Allah.

questions.question: In what area does the passage say he is also without equal besides law and worship?
questions.answer: In supplication and prayer.

questions.question: What broad subject does this passage focus on: political power, family life, or religious perfection?
questions.answer: Religious perfection.

questions.question: What six gifts or missions brought by the Prophet are said to be beyond comparison?
questions.answer: The sacred law, Islam, worship, the cause, the summons, and faith.

questions.question: How is the sacred law tested in the passage instead of being praised with empty words?
questions.answer: By pointing to its centuries-long rule over a large part of humanity.

questions.question: What three parts of the Prophet’s life are named as the source from which Islam appeared?
questions.answer: His deeds, his words, and his inner life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what did Islam become for millions of people every century?
questions.answer: Their guide, shelter, teacher, purifier, and means of growth.

questions.question: How did Islam help a person’s thinking?
questions.answer: It educated the mind.

questions.question: How did Islam help a person’s character and inner life?
questions.answer: It cleaned the heart and trained the soul.

questions.question: What made the Prophet’s worship different from that of others?
questions.answer: He practiced all its forms first and best.

questions.question: What shows that his worship was not shallow or rushed?
questions.answer: He observed it fully and paid attention to its deepest meanings.

questions.question: What challenge did he continue to face while maintaining worship?
questions.answer: Constant struggle and busy activity.

questions.question: How does the passage use the Jawshan al-Kabir as evidence?
questions.answer: It presents it as proof of his unmatched understanding of Allah in prayer.

questions.question: What does the comparison with later saints and knowers imply about his spiritual level?
questions.answer: His level was higher than all of theirs.

questions.question: What is being argued in “The Third” section about the Prophet’s message?
questions.answer: That what he brought is unique and unsurpassed.

questions.question: Which part of what he brought is described as managing society over a long period?
questions.answer: The sacred law.

questions.question: What two numbers help show the scale of that law’s impact?
questions.answer: One fifth of humanity and fourteen centuries.

questions.question: Why would those numbers matter in understanding the argument?
questions.answer: They show broad influence and long-lasting success.

questions.question: According to the passage, Islam came forth through what personal qualities or expressions of the Prophet?
questions.answer: Through his conduct, his speech, and his inward state.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam was for people’s minds?
questions.answer: A teacher and guide.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam was for people’s hearts?
questions.answer: A source of light and purification.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam was for people’s souls and spirits?
questions.answer: A training and refining force that helped them move forward.

questions.question: How is the Prophet described in relation to all the acts of worship in his religion?
questions.answer: He is described as the leading and earliest example in practicing them.

questions.question: What attitude toward Allah especially marked him in worship?
questions.answer: Deep piety and strong fear of Allah.

questions.question: What is impressive about the way he worshipped during times of struggle?
questions.answer: He still fulfilled worship completely and with deep attention.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying he combined the beginning and end of worship perfectly?
questions.answer: His servitude to Allah was complete from start to finish.

questions.question: What famous supplication is named in this section?
questions.answer: Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What does this supplication reveal about him according to the passage?
questions.answer: It reveals an unmatched level of knowledge of his Lord and accuracy in praising Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the Treatise on Supplicatory Prayer?
questions.answer: To point readers to an explanation that helps them see the unique greatness of the Jawshan.
